battle.name: 宜陽、汾北之戰
battle.brief: 公元569年（北周天和末年、陳太建元年），北齊與北周在河南、山西兩條邊線同時交鋒：北齊騎兵深入洛州南境宜陽，北周的兵鋒則抵汾水以北的河東。交戰以步卒楯陣與騎兵衝撞為主，卡面的羅馬方陣盾同年不可能在此，但它「盾緣咬合」的防線邏輯，正是兩軍步卒結陣拒騎的原型。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 這場戰爭發生在南北朝末期的三國格局之中，交戰的兩方是北周與北齊。北周以長安為京師，明帝宇文毓在位，年號天和；其國力承自西魏的府兵制：全國兵籍分屬各府，府下設團，兵農合一，按番上番，番次之間輪番更替，戰時集兵赴援，事罷歸農。北周的東方重鎮是洛州，治所在洛陽，另有並州治晉陽，控制河東與太原盆地；洛州總管與並州大將各領一方兵馬，軍械糧秣多由關中經河洛漕運下達。北齊以鄴城為都，幼主高湛在位，兵制是軍府與軍戶混編的軍府兵制，騎兵比例高於北周，番役以六品以下官員充任。宜陽在洛陽正南，是洛州最靠南的縣，北齊自河南與兗州方向南下，最先碰到的就是這一段；汾北則指汾水以北的河東北部，即並州與北齊分界的一帶，晉陽是這一線的樞紐。569年的形勢是：北周在洛州與並州兩面同時承受壓力，而北齊的野戰騎兵恰好能選擇弱點突破。這一戰的史書記載有限，交戰雙方在名冊上的番號、將領姓名多已散佚，可以確定的只有上述兩國的體系與兩處戰場的大致位置；同年在南方，陳朝正值太建元年，內部正在整頓，無力介入北方，因此這場衝突純粹是北方兩國之間的邊境交鋒。
countriesEn: This war took place in the late Three Kingdoms-era balance of power between north and south, and the two sides that fought were Northern Zhou and Northern Qi. Northern Zhou had its capital at Chang'an and was ruled by Emperor Ming, Yuwen Yu, whose reign era was Tianhe; its strength rested on the fubing system inherited from Western Wei, in which the military registers were distributed among the fu, each fu subdivided into tuan, soldiers and farmers were combined in one person, and units went into the field by rotation, returning to the fields between campaigns. Zhou's eastern anchor was Luozhou, seated at Luoyang, with Bingzhou at Jinyang controlling Hedong and the Taiyuan basin; the Luozhou zongguan and the Bingzhou general each commanded a district of its own, and arms and grain were sent down from Guanzhong along the Heluo waterway. Northern Qi sat at Ye City under the boy-emperor Gao Zhan; its army was a mixture of junfu and junhu households with a higher proportion of cavalry than Zhou, and its service rotations were filled by officials of the sixth rank and below. Yiyang lies due south of Luoyang and is the southernmost county of Luozhou, so a southward thrust out of Qi's Henan or Yanzhou directions would meet this stretch first; Fenbei, on the other hand, means the country north of the Fen River in northern Hedong, the border belt between Bingzhou and Qi, with Jinyang as its pivot. The situation in 569 was that Northern Zhou was under pressure on two fronts at once, Luozhou and Bingzhou, while Qi's field cavalry could pick exactly where to open a gap. The written record of this engagement is thin: the unit designations and commanders on both sides have largely been lost, and only the two systems described above and the rough position of the two battlefields can be established with confidence. In the south, the Chen court was in the first year of Taixian and was absorbed by internal reorganization, with no capacity to intervene in the north, so this clash was purely a border war between the two northern states.
people: 留下姓名的，以兩國的統治者與方面統帥為主。北周一方，明帝宇文毓在557年至570年間執政，此時已逐步把兵權從大冢宰宇文護手中收回，朝廷的實際軍務由大將軍楊堅一系主持；楊堅此時已是北周諸王之外最具軍權的重臣，他日後代周建隋，先平北齊再滅陳朝，都從這批北周軍隊起家。北齊一方，幼主高湛自565年即位，年紀尚輕，朝廷大權多歸外戚與權臣；河東戰線的主帥是大將斛律光，他自566年前後起都督並州諸軍事，長駐晉陽一帶，是北齊在汾水以北唯一能與北周相持的將領，其弟斛律羨領幽州，兄弟分鎮北疆，構成北齊北部防線的骨幹。北周方面，與斛律光相持的並州將領姓名沒有完整流傳，洛州一線的守將也僅見零星官職記載，雙方基層的隊長、弓手、輜重隊與工匠更無從查考。可以確定的還有南方的一條旁證：陳朝在太建元年正忙著重整侯瑱死後失去主帥的湘州軍系，沒有餘力北上，因此北周得以把洛州、並州兩區的兵力抽調應戰，也沒有第三方的干預使這場對峙提前結束。另可注意的是交戰雙方的年齡結構：北周的明帝宇文毓年近四十，正在收攏兵權；北齊的幼主高湛不過十餘歲，實權分散在斛律光等北疆將領與朝中權臣之間，這種權力分布使北齊在形勢有利時傾向於用邊境的小規模出擊來試探，而不願在調兵未成之前打一場全面戰爭。
peopleEn: The names that survive are chiefly those of the rulers and the front commanders of the two sides. On the Zhou side, Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu governed from 557 to 570 and by this time had already been drawing military authority back from the Grand Protector Yuwen Hu, the practical conduct of military affairs resting with the line of the Grand General Yang Jian; Yang Jian was already the heaviest weight among the Zhou princes in terms of military command, and he would later replace Zhou and found the Sui, first destroying Northern Qi and then the Chen, both beginning from precisely these Zhou formations. On the Qi side, the boy-emperor Gao Zhan had taken the throne in 566 while still a child, and power at court lay largely with consort kin and ministers; the commander on the Hedong front was the great general Hulu Guang, who from around 566 served as commander over the military of Bingzhou and was stationed for long years at Jinyang, the only Qi general able to hold his ground against Zhou north of the Fen River, while his brother Hulu Xian held Youzhou, the two brothers guarding the northern frontier in either hand as the backbone of Qi's northern defence. The names of the Zhou commanders who faced Hulu Guang at Bingzhou have not come down in full, nor those of the Luozhou garrison, and the ranks of the file, the archers, the baggage trains and the engineers are of course beyond recovery. One thing can be fixed on the southern side as well: the Chen court, in the first year of Taixian, was busy rebuilding the Xiangzhou command left leaderless by the death of Hou Zhen and had no strength to aid the north, so Zhou was able to draw troops out of the Luozhou and Bingzhou districts to meet the attack, and no third party intervened to end the deadlock early. The age structure of the opposing sides is also worth noting: Zhou's Emperor Ming Yuwen Yu was approaching forty and in the act of consolidating his grip on the army, while Qi's boy-emperor Gao Zhan was a child of barely ten, real power being dispersed between frontier commanders such as Hulu Guang and the ministers at court; such a distribution of authority inclined Qi toward small probing strikes across the border when the situation favoured it, and away from a general war before its mustering had been completed.
kits: 卡面上這件羅馬方陣盾，名號是 scutum，造於公元前一世紀的羅馬：凸面的長方盾，木框蒙皮，內層以木條夾持，外覆皮革，握把與橫桿在盾背。羅馬人用它組成密集的方陣前推，防線靠的是盾緣互相咬住、彼此支撐，而不是盾牌本身的厚度；一排盾接一排盾，形成整面可以承擔撞擊的活牆，後方的弩手與標槍手再從盾縫之後出手。這個兵器同年不可能出現在中原戰場上，羅馬的工藝與歐洲的兵制都與之無涉；它在同期中國的對位物是「楯」：野戰中步卒手持的圓盾與小楯，攻城與守城中用以遮蔽城頭、抵擋雲梯的「櫓」——蒙牛皮或夾板的大盾，高可過丈，須由兩三人合力持用。中原步卒結陣的邏輯與方陣盾一脈相承：以楯陣在前，以槊與環首刀壓住陣線，以蹶張弩與臂張弩在陣後覆射；騎兵衝上來時，盾手咬住盾緣，兩翼以長槊列拒馬，車兵與步兵混編的第二線才上來頂住缺口。雙方在具體裝備上仍有分別：北周步卒的甲以札甲為主，披鍑鍔、戴兜鍪，騎兵披札甲或魚鱗甲、用長槊與長刀；北齊的軍戶兵裝備較雜，亦有沿用前朝的兩當與褐衣者，騎兵同樣以槊刀為主。弩是雙方壓制騎兵與封鎖渡口的主力，蹶張弩的射程在二百至三百步，另有床弩與十字臂弩用於固定方向的封鎖；攻城則靠撞車、雲梯、飛樓與攻城塔。糧秣方面，北周的洛州與並州靠河洛與汾晉的漕運和屯田，北齊則倚鄴城周邊的糧道；冬天的草料供應，往往比兵員更早見底。
kitsEn: The card shows a Roman scutum, the type known as scutum, made in Rome in the first century BC: a convex rectangular shield of wood frame covered with hide, the inner face stiffened with strips of wood and the outside faced in leather, with the grip and the cross bar on the inside. The Romans formed it into the dense massed formation that advanced with shields locked edge to edge; the line depended on the rims biting into and supporting one another, not on the thickness of the boards, one rank of shields locking against the next to make a living wall able to absorb impact, while the archers and the javelin men behind shot out from behind the shield wall. No such weapon could stand on a Central Plains battlefield in the same year: the Roman craft and the European order of battle had nothing to do with this fight. Its counterpart in contemporary China was the xun, the shield: the small round shields and light shields carried by foot soldiers in the field, and the lu, the large hide-covered or laminated board used in siege and defence to mask the parapet and to turn away scaling ladders, taller than a man and needing two or three men to carry it. The logic of the Chinese infantry line ran directly parallel to the scutum: shields in front, spears and ring-pommel sabres pressing the line, crossbow-armed and drawn bowmen shooting over it; when cavalry came on, the shield-hands bit edge to edge, the flanks set long spears in a picket line, and only then would the second line of mixed cart and foot troops come up to close the gap. The two sides still differed in concrete equipment: Zhou's foot soldiers were armoured mainly in lamellar, with a lingjiudi over the body and a doumou on the head, and its cavalry wore lamellar or scale and used the long spear and the long sabre; Qi's junhu levies were more mixed, some still wearing the liangdang and brown cloth gear of the earlier dynasties, and its cavalry likewise fought with spear and sabre. The crossbow was the principal arm on both sides for checking cavalry and sealing fords, the drawn bow reaching two to three hundred paces, with bed crossbows and the cross-armed crossbow used to lock a fixed line; siege work relied on battering rams, scaling ladders, flying towers and siege towers. For supply, Zhou's Luozhou and Bingzhou drew on the waterways of Heluo and Fenjin together with military farms, while Qi relied on the grain roads around Ye City; in winter the fodder supply commonly ran out before the manpower did.
tactics: 兩條戰線的交鋒方式並不一樣。洛州一線的地形是典型的河洛塬地：宜陽在洛水與伊水交會之處，縣境內多黃土崗地與河灘，道路夾在丘陵與水渠之間，適合步卒設壘而不利大隊騎兵展開。北周守軍據宜陽城及沿線的壘塞，以弩陣封住通往洛陽的谷口，騎兵若強攻坡地，先要吃盡從坡頂傾瀉而下的箭，再撞上壘前的拒馬與鹿角，最後才碰到咬合的楯陣；真正吃虧的往往是失去節奏的攻方，馬隊在起伏地形上加速難、反衝難，一旦被弩幕覆蓋而散開，步卒再以長槊壓上，攻勢便垮。北齊另一方向的騎兵則走汾北：河東的汾水在冬季有結冰期，冰厚可踏時，騎兵可以從結冰的河道直接渡過，避開渡口的守備；北周在並州一線的部署因此以壘石為城，把重點放在各處渡口與津渡，一旦遇上薄冰，巡騎就得靠斥候在前面試冰，節奏極慢。兩線之間相隔數百里，調兵需十數日，北周只能靠河洛的漕運把洛州、汝州一線的兵馬與糧秣北運至並州，或反過來把河東的儲糧與馬匹南調，這條補給線一旦被北齊輕騎切斷，前線的持久作戰能力立刻下降。冬天還有別的麻煩：河洛多雨霧、泥濘，衝鋒速度與射程都受影響；汾北則是積雪沒膝，馬匹掉膘、弓弦發澀，弩的實際張力下降。在這樣的條件下，交戰多半不是一場決定性的會戰，而是反覆的試探與局部接觸：先以騎兵遮蔽與驅趕試探對方陣線的厚度，再在某一處局部投入優勢兵力，勝負往往在幾個時辰之內見分曉，隨即各自收兵。
tacticsEn: The two lines of contact did not fight in the same way. The terrain on the Luozhou line was typical Heluo loess country: Yiyang stands where the Luo and the Yi waters meet, the county full of loess ridges and river flats, its roads pinched between hills and irrigation channels, which suited foot soldiers laying fortified positions and did not suit a large body of cavalry trying to deploy. The Zhou defenders held the county seat of Yiyang and the fortified posts along the line, sealing the gaps that led up to Luoyang with crossbow volleys; cavalry attempting to force the slopes had first to swallow the arrows poured down from the ridge, then to smash into the cheval-de-frise and the deer-horn obstacles before the rampart, and only then meet the locked shield wall. The side that generally lost was the attacker who had lost his rhythm: horse troops found it hard to accelerate over broken ground and hard to recover momentum, and once they were covered by the crossbow fire and scattered, the foot soldiers closed with long spears and the attack collapsed. Qi's cavalry on the other axis moved through Fenbei, where the Fen River freezes in winter, and when the ice was thick enough to walk on, the horse could cross the frozen channel directly and avoid the defended fords; Zhou's deployment along Bingzhou was therefore built around stone-walled camps with the weight placed on the crossings and the ferries, and where the ice was thin the patrols had to send scouts ahead to test it, at a very slow pace. The two lines lay several hundred li apart and shifting troops between them took more than ten days, so Zhou could only move troops and grain from the Luozhou and Ruzhou lines north to Bingzhou along the Heluo waterway, or move the grain stores and horses of Hedong back to the south; if that supply line was cut by Qi's light horse, the ability of the front to sustain a long engagement collapsed at once. Winter brought other difficulties: Heluo was overcast and muddy, which reduced both the speed of a charge and the reach of the missile fire, while in Fenbei the snow lay deep enough to cover a man's knees, the horses fell out of condition and the bowstrings went slack and rough, so the actual tension of the crossbows fell away. Under such conditions the encounter was rarely one decisive battle but a series of probes and partial contacts: cavalry screens and driving attacks were used to test the thickness of the opposing line, superiority was then committed locally at one point, and the issue was usually settled within a few watches, after which each side withdrew.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。年份是公元569年，北周明帝天和末年，陳朝太建元年，北齊幼主高湛在位；交戰的月份在現存史籍中沒有明確記載，考慮河東冬季用兵的慣例與汾水的結冰期，本卡取正月，屬推算而非記載。地名上，宜陽在洛陽城正南約五十里，洛水自西來、伊水自西南來，兩水在縣境相會；宜陽縣的建置早於此役，漢魏以來一直是洛陽西南的屏障與驛道上的驛站，北周的洛州與陳朝、北齊的河南正面都以這一帶為分界。汾北不是一個縣名，而是指汾水以北的河東北部，涵蓋太原以北直到雁門一線的廣大山地，晉陽是這條線上最大的軍鎮，距洛陽數百里，騎兵順利也要數日。兵員方面，兩國在洛州與並州各有常備部署，但史籍沒有留下可以引用的出征數目，常見的說法只到概括的兵員記載；本卡因此不列具體兵數，只能說雙方在兩條戰線上投入的兵馬都是當地守軍加上中央調發的援兵，總量在數萬之譜，而一個月的消耗相當於半年的番役。器物尺度方面，羅馬方陣盾高約一公尺、寬約六十公分、蒙皮重數公斤；中國同期的櫓高可過丈，約合三公尺以上，必須兩三人合力；手持圓盾直徑多在三十公分上下；蹶張弩的有效射程在二百至三百步，約合三百至五百公尺。戰果數字沒有留下可靠記載：史籍只說兩線均有交鋒，未見確切的斬首、俘虜與器械損毀數目，因此本卡不引用任何具體斬獲。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are broadly as follows. The year is 569 CE, the last years of the Tianhe era under Emperor Ming of Zhou, the first year of Taixian in the Chen, with the boy-emperor Gao Zhan on the Qi throne; the month of the fighting is not explicitly recorded in the surviving histories, and given the winter campaigning custom of Hedong and the freezing of the Fen River this card takes the first month, which is an inference rather than a record. As for place names, Yiyang lies roughly fifty li due south of the city of Luoyang, the Luo coming from the west and the Yi from the southwest, the two waters meeting within the county; the county itself was established long before this war, and from the Han and Wei periods onward it was both a screen to the southwest of Luoyang and a relay station on the post road, with the Luozhou of Zhou and the Henan front of the Chen and the Qi all taking their dividing line around this stretch. Fenbei is not a county name but the country north of the Fen River in northern Hedong, covering the broad uplands from north of Taiyuan as far as the Yanmen line, Jinyang being the largest military town on that line, several hundred li from Luoyang and several days away even for horse. On manpower, both states had standing garrisons in Luozhou and Bingzhou, but the histories leave no usable figures for the size of the expedition, the usual formulations going no further than a general statement of troops engaged; this card therefore lists no precise numbers and can say only that the forces committed on both lines were the local garrisons reinforced by units dispatched from the centre, on an order of some tens of thousands in all, and that one month of this consumed what six months of peacetime service rotations would have. As for the scale of the objects, a Roman scutum stood about one metre high, was some sixty centimetres wide and weighed a few kilograms with its hide facing; the Chinese lu of the same period was taller than a man, roughly three metres or more, and had to be shouldered by two or three men; hand-held round shields ran to about thirty centimetres in diameter; and the drawn crossbow had an effective range of two to three hundred paces, some three hundred to five hundred metres. No reliable figures survive for the results: the histories record that there was fighting on both lines but give no exact counts of heads cut off, prisoners taken or equipment destroyed, so this card quotes no specific claim of kills.
cause: 打起來的起因可以分三層來看。第一層是北方的整體格局：西魏分家之後，北周在關中靠府兵制重建了兵源與財政的一致性，北齊則守著鄴城與河北、山東的膏腴之地，兩邊都想把河洛與河東這兩塊地方拿回來。河洛控著關中東出的門戶與漕運的終點，拿到洛州就等於在關中的門楣前架起一把刀；河東控著山西的馬匹、鹽鐵與太原的糧倉，拿到並州就等於掐住北齊西翼的脖子。566年前後兩國交換過洛州與晉陽的歸屬，邊界因此從洛陽城一線退到宜陽一線，從太原城一線退到汾北一線，兩條邊界都退到沒有天然屏障的地方，這種犬牙交錯的線最容易出事。第二層是569年這個時點的內政：北周明帝剛把兵權從大冢宰宇文護手中收回，宗室與權臣之間的猜忌未消，府兵番役正處在更替的空檔，關中的調兵需要時間；北齊幼主高湛年幼，斛律光兄弟坐鎮北疆，北齊內部則因河北的戶口與軍額問題而積著怨氣。第三層是北齊的戰略選擇：在北周內部空檔期，同時在宜陽與汾北兩處施壓，逼北周把有限的兵力拆成兩份；這也是為什麼此役以兩條戰線同時爆發的形式被記錄下來，而不是一場單一的會戰。南方沒有介入，是因為陳朝太建元年正在整頓湘州與荊州的兵備，侯瑱這一支能打的湘州軍剛失去主帥，沒有餘力北援；陳朝的存在只間接影響了北方，北周必須留一份兵力提防江淮不至於被趁虛而來。
causeEn: The outbreak can be read on three levels. The first is the overall shape of the north: after the split of Western Wei, Northern Zhou rebuilt in Guanzhong a single consistent system of recruitment and finance through the fubing, while Northern Qi held Ye City together with the rich lands of Hebei and Shandong, and each wanted to take back the two regions of Heluo and Hedong. Heluo controls the doorway through which Guanzhong looks east and the terminus of the grain transport, so to hold Luozhou is to set a blade against the lintel of Guanzhong; Hedong controls the horses, the salt and iron and the granary of Taiyuan, so to hold Bingzhou is to pinch the throat of Qi's western wing. Around 566 the two states exchanged the ownership of Luozhou and Jinyang, and the border retreated accordingly from the line of the city of Luoyang to the line of Yiyang, and from the line of the city of Taiyuan to the line of Fenbei; both borders were pushed back to ground with no natural screen, and a border of that interlocking kind is the one where trouble starts. The second level is the internal situation at this particular moment in 569: Zhou's Emperor Ming had only just drawn military power back from the Grand Protector Yuwen Hu, suspicion between the imperial clan and the ministers had not been settled, the fubing service rotations sat in a gap of turnover, and concentrating troops from Guanzhong took time; Qi had a child emperor, the Hulu brothers entrenched in the northern marches, and inside Qi the resentment of Hebei over the household registers and the military quotas had been accumulating. The third level is Qi's strategic choice: in the gap in Zhou's internal arrangements, pressure was applied at Yiyang and at Fenbei at one and the same time, forcing Zhou to split its limited force in two; this is why the engagement is recorded as flaring on two lines at once rather than as a single set-piece battle. The south did not intervene because the Chen court in the first year of Taixian was reorganising the defences of Xiangzhou and Jingzhou, and the Xiangzhou troops under Hou Zhen, the one body of men that could really fight, had just lost their commander and had no strength to come north; the presence of the Chen affected the north only indirectly, since Zhou had to keep a share of its forces watching the Jiang and Huai in case the south should move while it was pinned.
impact: 這場對峙沒有改變任何一條邊界線，但它留下的痕跡在往後十年裡都能看見。第一，北周在洛州與並州兩區的守備經此一役定型：宜陽以下的防線以城、壘、弩陣為骨架，汾北的防線則以津渡與斥候巡邏為骨架，這套部署一直用到北周滅齊的戰役，說明它在實戰裡站得住腳。第二，北齊兩線都沒有得手，卻在國力上付出了代價：此後數年北齊的府庫吃緊，河北的軍戶與官僚之間的矛盾積累，斛律光在北疆的權力越來越集中，成為朝廷無法迴避的威脅；高湛對斛律家的猜忌最終在577年爆發，斛律光及其諸子被誅，北齊的北方防線在滅齊前夜自行瓦解。第三，制度上的差距透過這一役顯露出來：北周的府兵能夠以集中的番役應付兩線作戰，北齊的軍府兵制卻需要更長的時間才能完成召集，兩者在持久戰與多線應戰上的差距逐漸累積；這條線索最終通向577年北周滅北齊、581年楊堅代周建隋、589年隋軍渡江滅陳的結局。就陳朝而言，這一役沒有直接影響，但它延後了北方兩國互相消耗的過程，替南朝多留了二十年的喘息時間，也讓陳朝得以在太建年間完成北線的整軍；到隋軍渡江的時候，陳朝已經沒有可以與北方抗衡的北向機動兵。
impactEn: This standoff changed no border line, but its traces can be seen for the whole of the following decade. First, the defences of Zhou in the Luozhou and Bingzhou districts were settled by this war: the line below Yiyang was built on a skeleton of walled towns, earthworks and crossbow positions, while the line at Fenbei was built on a skeleton of ferries and scouting patrols, and that deployment was still in use through the Zhou campaigns that destroyed Qi, which shows that it stood up in actual fighting. Second, Qi gained nothing on either line but paid for it in national strength: in the years that followed the Qi treasury grew tight, the friction between the military households of Hebei and the officials of the capital accumulated, and the concentration of Hulu Guang's authority in the northern marches became a threat the court could no longer avoid; Gao Zhan's suspicion of the Hulu family finally broke out in 577, Hulu Guang and his sons were put to death, and the northern defence of Qi collapsed of its own accord on the eve of the state's destruction. Third, the difference between the two systems showed through this war: the Zhou fubing could meet a two-front war with concentrated service rotations, while the Qi junfu system needed a far longer time to complete its mustering, and the gap between them in protracted and multi-axis warfare accumulated steadily; that thread leads on to the destruction of Northern Qi by Zhou in 577, to Yang Jian's replacement of Zhou and the founding of Sui in 581, and to the Sui crossing the Yangtze and ending the Chen in 589. As for the Chen, this war had no direct effect, but it postponed the mutual exhaustion of the two northern states, bought the southern court another twenty years of breathing space, and gave the Chen time to complete the reorganization of its northern line during the Taixian years; by the time the Sui army crossed the river, the Chen no longer had any mobile force in the north with which to answer the north.
result: 就現存線索可以確定的部分而言，結果是沒有結果：宜陽沒有被北齊攻下，汾北也沒有被北周突破，雙方在兩個方向上互相頂住，各自收兵，邊界維持原狀，北齊的兩路攻勢都停在北周的堡壘與壘塞之前。這場戰爭在史籍中的記載十分零星，能確定的只有三件事：發生的年份是569年；交火的地點有兩處，一處是洛州南境的宜陽，一處是河東汾水以北的汾北；交火發生在北周與北齊同時在兩條邊境施壓的格局之中。將帥的姓名、兵力的確數、斬獲與俘虜的數目、以及戰術的細節，都沒有留下可靠的記載，因此本卡所述只到骨架為止，戰術與裝備部分的推論成分較多，必須以當時北周的府兵番役、並州的壘城體系、以及河洛到河東的漕運距離為依據，而不是以某一部史籍的原文為依據。戰後的走向則相當清楚：北周把力量集中到北方，於575至577年間滅北齊；北齊在失去北方屏障與一批名將之後迅速崩解；北周在578年由武帝宇文邕即位後也未能延續，581年楊堅受禪代周，建立隋朝；589年隋軍渡江，陳朝亡。宜陽與汾北的兩處堡壘與渡口，後來都成為隋軍北伐與南下時的著力點：這場沒有勝負的邊境戰，實際上把隋朝統一南北時的戰略骨架，先一步在河洛與河東的地面上畫了出來。
resultEn: So far as the surviving clues allow, the result is that there was no result: Yiyang was not taken by Northern Qi, Fenbei was not broken by Northern Zhou, the two sides held one another at both axes, each withdrew, the border stood where it had stood, and both of Qi's drives halted before the fortified towns and earthworks of Zhou. The record of this war in the histories is extremely scattered, and only three things can be fixed: the year, 569; the two places where the fighting occurred, one at Yiyang on the southern edge of Luozhou and one at Fenbei north of the Fen River in Hedong; and the circumstance that the fighting took place in a situation where Zhou and Qi were pressing on two border lines at once. The names of the commanders, the exact numbers of troops, the counts of kills and prisoners, and the tactical details have left no reliable record, so what follows here reaches only as far as the skeleton, and the tactical and equipment portions carry a larger inferential element, resting on the fubing rotations of Northern Zhou, on the fortified-town system of Bingzhou, and on the transport distance from Heluo to Hedong, rather than on the text of any single history. The course of events after the war, by contrast, is clear: Zhou concentrated its strength northward and destroyed Northern Qi between 575 and 577; Qi fell apart quickly once it had lost its northern screen and a number of its leading generals; Zhou itself did not outlast the accession of Emperor Wu Yuwen Yong in 578, and in 581 Yang Jian received the abdication and founded the Sui; in 589 the Sui army crossed the river and the Chen was ended. The fortified towns and crossings at Yiyang and Fenbei later became the points of effort for the Sui armies both in the north and in the south: this border war that settled nothing in fact drew out in advance, on the ground of Heluo and Hedong, the strategic skeleton by which the Sui would one day unify the country.
